subject: gastric-brooding frog
title: This Frog Swallowed Her Eggs and Gave Birth Through Her Mouth

scenes.text: This frog ate her own eggs. Six weeks later, she spat out frogs.
The gastric-brooding frog of Queensland, Australia. After the male fertilised her eggs, the mother swallowed them whole.
Her stomach should have digested them. But the egg jelly carried a hormone, prostaglandin E2, that switched off her stomach acid.
For at least six weeks she ate nothing. Her stomach swelled until it filled her body, her lungs deflated, and she breathed through her skin.
Then 21 to 26 fully formed froglets climbed out of her mouth. Disturb her, and she'd vomit the whole brood out at once.
Last seen in the wild in 1983. In 2013, scientists cloned its embryos from frozen tissue. They never got past the first stage.

description:
The gastric-brooding frog swallowed her fertilised eggs, raised them in her stomach for at least six weeks, and gave birth to fully formed froglets through her mouth.
Two species of Rheobatrachus lived in Queensland, Australia. Prostaglandin E2 in the egg jelly, and later in the tadpoles' gill mucus, switched off the mother's hydrochloric acid production, so her stomach stopped digesting. She did not eat while brooding; her stomach grew until it filled her body cavity, her lungs deflated and she relied on breathing through her skin. Broods of 21 to 26 juveniles were recorded, and a disturbed mother could expel all of them in a single act of propulsive vomiting. The southern species was last seen in 1983, the northern in 1987, and both are listed as extinct. In 2013 the Lazarus Project cloned embryos using frozen tissue, but they did not survive beyond the early embryo stage.
Should scientists keep trying to bring it back?
first_comment: Her stomach stopped making acid for six weeks so the babies could grow. Which extinct animal would you bring back first?
